newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA GOES FOR GOLD WITH NEW MANDELA MEDALLION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA GOES FOR GOLD WITH NEW MANDELA MEDALLION.

text.p: The South African Mint struck gold on Tuesday, launching the second series of the Nelson Mandela Presidential Medallion to raise two million rand to help educate the country's disadvantaged population.
Depicting Mandela's bust on one side and a child studying on the other, the 14,100 coins will be sold to collectors and are seen bringing in the same revenue as the first series.

"The significance of having President Mandela's image on the medallion goes a long way to show his support for education. The profits go entirely to education in southern Africa," said James Urdang, executive director of Education Africa, a non-governmental organisation commissioning the medallion.
The medal's similarity to the country's other gold money, the well-known Kruger Rand, is limited to the fact that both are the namesakes of South African presidents.

While Kruger Rands are legal tender, the Mandela coin -- 24 carat gold -- is purely commemorative and although it might become a much sought-after item, considering Mandela's international status, it can never buy anything, Urdang said.
The first series of Mandela Medallions was struck 20 months ago and Urdang said Education Africa, together with the South African Mint, hope to strike a new series every year.
The second series makes available 14,100 gold medallions containing varying ounces of the metal. Education Afrcia hopes to raise about two million rand from the sale of the coins.
A hundred five ounce medallions have been struck, 2,000 one ounce medallions, 2,000 medallions of a quarter of an ounce and 10,000 medallions of a tenth of an ounce of gold.
